title: A DESK THAT NEVER SLEEPS
note: Figures and quotes are from the Alaska Business feature A Front Desk That Never Sleeps (September 28th). The trading post, the bell and the Auditor are illustrations, not real businesses or people.

lines.text: It's two in the morning. Somebody rings the front desk, and nobody's there.
lines.t: It's two in the morning. Somebody rings the front desk, and nobody's there.

lines.text: Alaska Business magazine says small businesses are buying A I front desks. Steve Vick's Fairbanks firm, Web nine oh seven, builds them. He calls it a desk that never sleeps.
lines.t: Alaska Business magazine says small businesses are buying A I front desks. Steve Vick's Fairbanks firm, Web nine oh seven, builds them. He calls it a desk that never sleeps.

lines.text: North Pole guide Rod Pangborn, a Web nine oh seven client, calls his chatbot scary good. He estimates five to ten percent of customers use it.
lines.t: North Pole guide Rod Pangborn, a Web nine oh seven client, calls his chatbot scary good. He estimates five to ten percent of customers use it.

lines.text: Another Web nine oh seven job, an emergency vet service. At midnight, a worried owner calls one number, and a calm voiced A I says who's on call.
lines.t: Another Web nine oh seven job, an emergency vet service. At midnight, a worried owner calls one number, and a calm voiced A I says who's on call.

lines.text: Vick says it's just reading a spreadsheet. To the caller, it's panic turning to relief.
lines.t: Vick says it's just reading a spreadsheet. To the caller, it's panic turning to relief.

lines.text: But Carlos Machuca, of the Alaska Small Business Development Center, calls the common mistake accidental adoption. A free chatbot, turned on, with no plan.
lines.t: But Carlos Machuca, of the Alaska Small Business Development Center, calls the common mistake accidental adoption. A free chatbot, turned on, with no plan.

lines.text: Out of the box, Vick says, a model will confidently make up an answer.
lines.t: Out of the box, Vick says, a model will confidently make up an answer.

lines.text: So, a trend or one firm's showcase? Both stories are Web nine oh seven jobs. The five to ten percent is one owner's estimate. The feature reports no count of wrong answers.
lines.t: So, a trend or one firm's showcase? Both stories are Web nine oh seven jobs. The five to ten percent is one owner's estimate. The feature reports no count of wrong answers.

lines.text: The article says Web nine oh seven tests with awkward, hyper local questions.
lines.t: The article says Web nine oh seven tests with awkward, hyper local questions.

lines.text: But Machuca says the owner with no plan is the one he commonly sees.
lines.t: But Machuca says the owner with no plan is the one he commonly sees.

lines.text: So the trend is unproven. The win and the warning are one rule. The bot shines where somebody wrote the answer down.
lines.t: So the trend is unproven. The win and the warning are one rule. The bot shines where somebody wrote the answer down.

lines.text: Machuca's rule, if getting it wrong would cost you a customer permanently, keep a human in that loop.
lines.t: Machuca's rule, if getting it wrong would cost you a customer permanently, keep a human in that loop.

lines.text: Which question would you never let a bot answer alone, and which is just a spreadsheet?
